items.title: Cashing Out a Pension or Taking the Monthly Check? The Dividend Answer for a $610,000 Lump Sum
items.summary: A $610,000 pension lump sum sounds like freedom, but the monthly check comes with a guarantee that a dividend portfolio simply cannot replicate. Before you sign anything, there are three numbers that expose which choice actually leaves you better off.

items.title: What a $1.55 Million Portfolio Actually Pays After Taxes, Medicare Premiums, and Reality
items.summary: A seven-figure portfolio looks like security until federal taxes, Medicare surcharges, Social Security phase-ins, and inflation each take their share. What actually clears into your checking account from $1.55 million depends on decisions most retirees never see coming.

items.title: This $1.75 Million Portfolio Pays $10,200 a Month From Three Income Buckets
items.summary: Chasing a 7% blended yield across a $1.75 million portfolio sounds straightforward until you realize that loading up on the highest payers quietly destroys the very income stream you built. Three buckets solve the problem in ways that a single fund simply cannot.

items.title: Build Monthly Income With These 3 Bulletproof Dividend Stocks
items.summary: Three quarterly dividend payers from the S&P 500 can cover every calendar month without touching a single REIT or BDC, and one of them has sent shareholders a check every year since Woodrow Wilson was president.

items.title: Procter & Gamble Has Raised Its Dividend for 70 Straight Years. Here's How Much $25,000 Invested Pays Annually.
items.summary: The yield is just average, but patient investors are still being well rewarded.

items.title: When Inflation Is Sticky, 5 Dividend Aristocrats Are the Stocks to Own Now and Forever
items.summary: Sticky inflation is quietly rewarding a specific group of stocks with decades of uninterrupted dividend growth, and Wall Street's top analysts say five of them are built to profit no matter how long rising prices persist.

items.title: Procter & Gamble (PG) Pushes Charmin And Swiffer, Is It Trading At A Premium?
items.summary: Procter & Gamble (PG) is back in consumer headlines after fresh marketing pushes from Charmin and Swiffer, including the Charmin Forever Roll and Swiffer Hair Magnet, just ahead of the back to college shopping season. These product pushes arrive as Procter & Gamble’s share price edges to US$145.40, with a modest gain on a year-to-date basis but a decline in the 1-year total shareholder return. This suggests recent momentum has softened, even as long-term total shareholder returns remain...

items.title: Dividends vs. an Annuity: Which Turns $840,000 Into More Monthly Income for Life?
items.summary: A nest egg of $840,000 sits right at the crossroads where dividends and annuities each look surprisingly compelling, and where the wrong choice quietly costs you tens of thousands of dollars over a 20-year retirement.
